title_prefix: VERSION user agent has neither Core's 25
mechanism: CONFIRMED end to end through the SHIPPED handshake, not just the codec. src/serialization/message-macro.lisp:114-116 defines :var-string as (map 'string #'code-char (br-read-var-bytes br)) with no length limit and no character filter; src/serialization/messages.lisp:204 gives version-message its user-agent field through that row. The live inbound path is perform-inbound-handshake (src/networking/peer.lisp:1233) -> %receive-and-store-version (:1097), which stores the string verbatim at :1114-1116 ((peer-user-agent peer) (bl.ser:version-message-user-agent version-msg)). The only bound is the 24-byte header's payload-length check in receive-message (src/networking/peer.lisp:625-631) against bl:+max-message-payload+ = 4,000,000 (src/config.lisp:298), so a VERSION payload of exactly 4,000,000 bytes is accepted and only 4,000,001 disconnects. A version payload with an empty user agent is 86 bytes, so the admissible user agent runs to about 3,999,910 bytes. From there the raw string reaches debug.log at src/node/listen.lisp:44-47 and src/node/peers.lisp:569, and getpeerinfo's "subver" at src/rpc/net.lisp:240 ((or (bl.net:peer-user-agent peer) "")). Core instead reads subVer through LIMITED_STRING(strSubVer, MAX_SUBVERSION_LENGTH) (refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:3640), which THROWS 'String length limit exceeded' above MAX_SUBVERSION_LENGTH = 256 (refs/bitcoin/src/net.h:67, LimitedStringFormatter::Unser at refs/bitcoin/src/serialize.h:614-625), and stores only SanitizeString(strSubVer) (:3641), whose SAFE_CHARS_DEFAULT is alphanumerics plus " .,;-_/:?@()" (refs/bitcoin/src/util/strencodings.cpp:20-39) - newline, CR, ESC and every non-ASCII byte are dropped at the boundary. Grep confirms our tree has no SanitizeString equivalent for inbound text: 'sanitize' in src/ matches only miniscript's ms-sanitize-type and our OWN outbound -uacomment check (src/config/values.lisp:154).
consequence: REAL, S2 confirmed on two independent consequences, neither of which needs authentication. (1) LOG-LINE FORGERY. %log-escape-message (src/logging.lisp:100-115) is a faithful port of Core's BCLog::LogEscapeMessage: it renders control characters as \\xNN but deliberately passes newline through. Executed against Core's SanitizeString semantics, the answer to 'does our escaper already cover what SanitizeString strips' is NO - SanitizeString drops a strict superset (newline included), and newline is precisely the byte it must drop for the escaper to be sufficient. Rendering listen.lisp's real format string through bl.log::format-log-entry with an attacker user agent produced THREE lines from one call, lines 2 and 3 being entirely attacker-written and indistinguishable from genuine node output ('[net] Shutdown: done', '[net] New outbound peer connected: version: 70016, blocks=1, peer=9'). The tree's own functional-test oracle greps debug.log for exactly such lines, so a monitor, an assert_debug_log scraper or an operator alert can be driven by a remote peer. The ESC byte WAS escaped (\\x1b present, no raw ESC in the entry), so terminal-escape injection is already closed; the newline is the open half. (2) MEMORY. The stored user agent is an SBCL (simple-array character (*)), i.e. FOUR bytes of heap per attacker byte: measured 15,980,112 bytes retained for a 3,995,021-character user agent that completed the handshake. With bitcoin-lisp::*max-inbound-connections* = 114 that is about 1.82 GB of live heap held by 114 connections that need only upload ~456 MB once, and every getpeerinfo call re-serializes all of it (a 100,000-character subver encodes to 100,013 JSON bytes, so ~456 MB per response). REFUTER'S QUESTIONS ANSWERED: the 4,000,000-byte cap DOES bound a single message, so this is not unbounded growth and I do not raise it to S1 - the ceiling is the inbound slot count times 16 MB. NOTHING rate-limits or punishes it: check-peer-rate-limit (src/networking/peer.lisp:1868) consults a per-command token bucket only for commands that carry a :rate-bucket, and it is called ONLY from handle-message (src/networking/protocol.lisp:154), the post-VERACK dispatch loop; a VERSION is consumed inside the handshake and never reaches that call, so there is no ban, no discouragement and no misbehaviour score for a 4 MB subversion string. The handshake itself completed successfully (:HANDSHAKE-OK T) in both runs, so the peer keeps its slot.
evidence: All probes ran in the pinned project container (bitcoin-lisp-sbcl:2.6.5-4, SBCL 2.6.5.HEAD.1-85913ed) through cl-workbench repl eval; the probe file drove the SHIPPED functions (open-listener -> accept-connection -> make-inbound-peer -> perform-inbound-handshake on one thread, make-tcp-connection + send-bytes + flush-send-buffer on the other). (1) 300 KB run: (:HANDSHAKE-OK T :PAYLOAD-LEN 300154 :MAX-PAYLOAD 4000000 :SENT-UA-LEN 300064 :STORED-UA-LEN 300064 :IDENTICAL T :STORED-NEWLINES 2 :STORED-TYPE (SIMPLE-ARRAY CHARACTER (300064)) :BYTES-RETAINED 1200272). (2) At the cap: (:HANDSHAKE-OK T :PAYLOAD-LEN 3995111 :MAX-PAYLOAD 4000000 :SENT-UA-LEN 3995021 :STORED-UA-LEN 3995021 :IDENTICAL T :STORED-NEWLINES 1 :BYTES-RETAINED 15980112). (3) Cap boundary through read-message-header: (:DECLARED 4000001 :CAP 4000000 :OVER-CAP-P T :EMPTY-VERSION-PAYLOAD-LEN 86). (4) Log forgery through bl.log::format-log-entry on listen.lisp's own control string: (:LINES 3 :LINE1 "[2026-09-05 11:49:01] Inbound peer 203.0.113.7 (/Satoshi:27.0/" :LINE2 "2026-09-05T12:00:00Z [net] Shutdown: done" :LINE3 "2026-09-05T12:00:01Z [net] New outbound peer connected: version: 70016, blocks=1, peer=9\\x1b[31m) handshake complete" :ESC-ESCAPED 193 :RAW-ESC-PRESENT NIL). (5) getpeerinfo cost and slot count: (:UA-LEN 100000 :JSON-LEN 100013 :RETAINED-STRING-BYTES 400016 :MAX-INBOUND 114). Ours: src/serialization/message-macro.lisp:114-116; src/serialization/messages.lisp:204; src/networking/peer.lisp:1097-1116 (%receive-and-store-version), :625-631 (the only cap), :1233-1271 (perform-inbound-handshake), :1868-1876 (check-peer-rate-limit); src/networking/protocol.lisp:154 (its only caller); src/config.lisp:298; src/node/listen.lisp:44-47; src/node/peers.lisp:569; src/rpc/net.lisp:240; src/logging.lisp:100-115. Core: refs/bitcoin/src/net.h:67; refs/bitcoin/src/net_processing.cpp:3638-3642; refs/bitcoin/src/serialize.h:493 and :614-625; refs/bitcoin/src/util/strencodings.cpp:20-39.
fix_shape: Port Core's two boundary layers, in Core's order, at the one place the string enters the process. First, cap the read: give the :var-string codec row (or a new :limited-string row that takes a limit) the LIMITED_STRING behaviour - read the CompactSize length, and if it exceeds the field's limit signal a deserialization error rather than allocating, so the version message's user-agent field is declared with Core's 256-byte MAX_SUBVERSION_LENGTH and an oversized VERSION fails to parse and drops the peer through the existing bad-message path instead of being stored. Doing it in the codec, not in %receive-and-store-version, is what stops the next peer-supplied string field from inheriting the gap. Second, add a SanitizeString equivalent in the util layer with Core's three rule sets (SAFE_CHARS_DEFAULT, SAFE_CHARS_UA_COMMENT, SAFE_CHARS_FILENAME), and apply the DEFAULT rule to the subversion at the same point Core does - store the sanitized form on the peer, so the log line, getpeerinfo's "subver" and anything else reading peer-user-agent all get the cleaned string with no further work; keep %log-escape-message exactly as it is, since it is a correct port of LogEscapeMessage and the newline pass-through is only safe once the boundary filter exists. Core also wraps every log line that prints a peer-supplied message type in SanitizeString (net.cpp:761, :821, :828 and net_processing.cpp:3582, :3817, :4017, :5167, :5284-5286), so the same helper should be applied to the command name in our 'received: ~A' line and in the bad-magic/oversized/incomplete/checksum warnings, which today print an unfiltered 12-byte command field. Tests: a version message with a 257-byte user agent must fail to deserialize; one with 256 must succeed; a user agent containing LF, CR and ESC must come back with all three removed; and a positive control asserting the sanitizer actually drops a byte, so the check cannot go vacuous. NOT IMPLEMENTED - verdict only.
